svg.title: One statement, five sides
svg.desc: A grid of 38 articles by five sides. Filled in: Why 37, In action 37, Practice 35, When it breaks 32, If I doubt it 19.
svg.text: Every article looks at its statement from the same five sides; a dot is a side with something in it, a ring a
side left empty with a reason.

g.title: Article 20 · Why: No passage in this section says why I should take things apart; the section gives the method and not its reason.

svg.text: What follows for what I do.

g.title: Article 30 · In action: No passage in this section says what I should do because things are the same and foul; it asks me only to see them so, and to feel about them as I feel at the games and the baths.

Article 3 · Practice: No passage used in this article gives an exercise: Asclepius and his orders in 5.8 are a comparison, not something to do, and 3.12, set aside, has one (to say of each thing where it comes from) but its subject is judging impressions.
Article 29 · Practice: No passage in this section gives an exercise to repeat.
Article 33 · Practice: No passage in this section gives an exercise to repeat; they describe what happens to what I am made of.

svg.text: What failing looks like, and the way

g.title: Article 4 · When it breaks: No passage in this section describes losing sight of this, or recovering it.
Article 5 · When it breaks: No passage in this section describes failing at one’s purpose.
Article 20 · When it breaks: No passage in this section describes what failing at this looks like or the way back.
Article 23 · When it breaks: No passage in this section describes losing hold of my reason or my attention, or the way back; 6.32 only calls the first shocking.
Article 29 · When it breaks: No passage in this section says what failing at these rules looks like or how to come back.
Article 33 · When it breaks: No passage in this section describes what failing looks like here or how to come back from it.

svg.text: What still holds if the statement is

g.title: Article 1 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section considers that reasoning beings might not be one; the doubt is taken up under Article 3.
Article 2 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section asks what remains if reason is not what a human being is for.
Article 6 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section considers that what the whole brings might not be good for me; the article states the trust and does not argue for it.
Article 9 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section asks what holds if keeping these names is not enough, or if the gods ask something else.
Article 12 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section asks what still holds if I cannot retreat into myself, or if my mind is not my own.

Article 14 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section asks what still holds if there are no gods; 12.21 answers those who ask where Marcus has seen them with grounds for revering them, which stand under Why.
Article 16 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section considers what would still hold if my happiness were not decided in my own soul, so Marcus gives nothing under this label.
Article 18 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section asks what holds if a good state of soul and good actions are not enough for me, or if nothing gives and takes back.
Article 20 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section asks what would remain if things could not be taken apart in this way.
Article 21 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section asks what holds if wiping out impressions and checking impulses were not in my power.
Article 22 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section asks what still holds if acting well whatever others say, or changing only for reasons, were wrong.
Article 23 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section asks what still holds if my reason deserves no more respect than a craft does.
Article 24 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section asks what holds if living cannot be trained like a skill, or if reason is not enough for it.
Article 25 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section considers what holds if going back does not steady me or if the work stays hard to bear.
Article 26 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section asks what still holds if I was not made for this work or if questioning my actions does no good.
Article 28 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section asks what still holds if another person’s wrong could harm me after all.
Article 29 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section asks what still holds if these rules are wrong.
Article 30 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section asks what holds if things are not always the same or not foul; the article states this way of seeing and does not argue for it.
Article 37 · If I doubt it: No passage in this section asks what would hold if these lessons were wrong; Book 1 gives thanks and does not argue.

svg.text: Figure 5 · How the Constitution was made
